label: conj:crystal-graph-realization
title: Hecke normal forms realise crystal highest-weight vectors
html:
Conjecture (crystal-graph realisation of Hecke normal forms). Let K be a closed braid with Hecke normal form T_w \in H_n(R, q). Under the Brundan–Kleshchev isomorphism [brundankleshchev2009], the Gröbner–Shirshov canonical basis element T_w corresponds to an indecomposable graded projective KLR module. This module is a highest-weight vector of the Kashiwara crystal \mathrm{Cryst}(\mathfrak{sl}_n) [kashiwara1991]. It satisfies \tilde e_i \cdot T_w = 0 for every Kashiwara raising operator \tilde e_i.

Computational shortcut. The GS reduction engine can be replaced by a directed traversal on the crystal graph. Starting from the input word and recursively applying \tilde e_i operators, the procedure terminates at T_w. The relevant component of \mathrm{Cryst}(\mathfrak{sl}_n) is finite. Termination is immediate; no S-polynomial overlap analysis is required. The plactic-monoid bridge [lecouvey2007] certifies that the GS irreducible forms and crystal highest-weight vertices are in bijection.

The literature establishes the Brundan–Kleshchev isomorphism and the bijection for generic Hecke and KLR algebras. It remains conjectural that our specific GS reduction order matches the canonical basis labels under Brundan–Kleshchev for the QOU ansatz. We verify this match empirically on the witnessed normal forms. A rigorous proof requires formalising the GS reduction order inside the KLR diagrammatic calculus.

We use this conjecture to upgrade the heuristic confinement filtration to a \mathbb{Z}-graded KLR shift. We also use it to explain the GS engine's homological pruning. The conjecture replaces a class of brute-force S-polynomial bounds rather than an existing proof.
heading: Conjecture
